newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan plans gasoline benzene content cut from 2000.
newsitem.headline: Japan plans gasoline benzene content cut from 2000.

text.p: Japan is planning to implement stricter environmental standards on the benzene content of gasoline from early 2000, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.
"Plans are to restrict the benzene content in gasoline to less than one percent for all shipments," a MITI official said, adding that a final decision would be made on October 23.
The current ceiling on the benzene content of gasoline is five percent.
MITI is also planning to stiffen guidelines on the sulphur content in gas oil, which is mainly used by buses and trucks, to below 0.05 percent from October 1997, the official said.
Current standards allow up to 0.2 percent of sulphur.
"An agreement on the sulphur content standards has not yet been reached among all parties involved," he said.
A conclusion is expected in a month's time, he said.
The oil industry has been preparing for the stricter quality guidelines on oil products by upgrading existing facilities or constructing new units.
The new standards had been widely anticipated, but specific deadlines had not been known.
